column1: # Mario Kart World (Switch 2). In bring-up: the base game (SDK 19.3.3 built for the Switch 2, Ounce); update 1.8.0 (SDK 21.4.0) is packed from a profile derived from this one
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive, Havok, Pia), NVN2 (Ampere shaders).
# Packed from a dump folder (base/, updates/<version>/) with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).
# The Mac app declares LSSupportsGameMode. On the 16-core M2 Pro this profile was tuned on, Game Mode cost nothing in fullscreen (one host in two bundles, with and without
# a gaming session: the same frame rates, GPU time within 2 %) and did not hold the GPU's clock down (docs/reference/frame-rate.md, macOS Game Mode holds the GPU at its
# lowest clock, "Another chip"); by Apple's description it also doubles the Bluetooth sampling rate of controllers. off for a Mac where the clock falls
# The Mac window starts in fullscreen: every run of the final build was measured there (built-in screen, switched to a fixed 60 Hz), and Game Mode needs it.
# The settings window's Display mode and DM_FULLSCREEN choose otherwise
# Update 1.8.0 (v917504) is packed from a profile derived from this one. A dump has no control data, so the display version comes from here: the app's version
# and what the game's GetDisplayVersion answers (main's build ID of 1.8.0 = 1.8.0)
# 1.8.0 is the build this profile's frame rate work was measured on (mkw/README.md), so a build of it is reported as tested instead of with the warning for a version the
# profile was not brought up on; the SDK-wide patches that match nothing in it (sdk_patches.py: Unity's stream buffer, the address region rules) stay in the match tables
# The base game's subsdk0 is a Mono runtime (nn::ecli); 1.8.0's subsdk0 is the movie player and its subsdk1 a C library (build IDs from pull request #1116, not checked here).
# Each build row names its own modules, and the host loads those of main's build (main.c profile_modules)
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on:
# nninitStartup still sets a heap of pool - used (SetHeapSize 0x1dbc00000, 7.43 GB, with the 9 GB pool; 1.8.0 asks 0x1de400000, 7.47 GB, by pull request #1116), and nnMain allocates a fixed
# 7.04 GB block from it: 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 8 GB heap region
# MapPhysicalMemory past the application pool fails, as on Horizon (hle_svc.c): the game's streaming frees its own blocks instead of mapping more (README, Memory in free roam)
# No twin samplers, and the NaN coordinate guard off the cube samples (dmsh_build.py border_emu, nan_coord_fmax with cube: a cube direction keeps no guard, a cube array keeps it on
# its layer, the 2D and array guards stay as translated, which dmsh_fetch.fold matches). PR #1230: on an M1 Pro the per-sample border branch and the coordinate NaN select kept the
# samples from overlapping (the cube prefilter 4744589bb8f9f7dd: 2.2 → 0.7 ms a chain; title screen, alternating runs, with fmax: GPU p50 27.0–27.8 → 18.3–19.5 ms a frame). On the
# 16 GB M2 Pro the cube and cube array filters took 3 to 9 % less in a Metal harness (2026-11-13). No run printed a border colour Metal lacks (title, menus, the Mushroom Cup's four races)
# The framework picks each frame's interval (1 or 2 vsyncs, which the game steps by) from the frame's CPU time alone, so frames that wait on the GPU kept interval 1 and played in
# slow motion. The interval takes the host's frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it), at most 2; the game's own
# The stub hands the game at most 2, so the host's frame step holds and pays back with at most 2 as well (nvn_fstep.h step_max): at hold 3 the game ran at two thirds of its speed
# A late frame does not lengthen the hold of the frames after it (the final build's setting; DM_FPS_HOLD and the launcher's Hold frames when late override it)
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here, to be confirmed on this game
# Render pipelines are compiled whole, with their colour state: specialized from a base that leaves it open, the first reflection map's filter (4744589bb8f9f7dd) ran three
# times slower on the GPU (M2 Pro, 1.8.0, a race: GPU time 14.1 -> 12.4-12.9 ms, late presents 39-48 -> 0.7-6 a minute; README, "Frame rate")
# The reflection maps' filters write the six faces of a cube map level from one fragment shader, 32 samples a face (765844f5609bb11b a cube array's, 4744589bb8f9f7dd a
# cube's), into targets of 64x64 (console mode; 32x32 in handheld mode) down to 1x1: one invocation computes all six, and on such a target that is what the pass costs.
# Up to 64x64 a listed shader's draw runs as one layered pass, a draw a face (DM_NVN_FS_LAYER, on by default). Until its face pipelines are built, and with
# DM_NVN_FS_LAYER=0, it is drawn once for each face up to the size given here, which a pipeline compiled whole turns into one face's part: each filter up to the size at
# which that pays (M2 Pro: the cube array filter up to 64x64, the cube filter up to 8x8; README, "Frame rate")
# Metal's encoding on a thread of its own: in split screen the replay thread translates up to 11,000 draws a frame, and encoding them itself was 3 ms of the 27 a frame
# took it with four players (M2 Pro; a race with one player is unchanged). DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD and the launcher's Encode thread override it
# The settings the final build was measured with (2026-11-14, a 16 GB M2 Pro; mkw/README.md, mkw/TRIAGE.md), as this profile's defaults: the launcher shows them and
# Reset to tested defaults goes back to them, and the matching DM_ variable overrides each.
# MetalFX scales the picture up to the window or the screen (DM_PRESENT_UPSCALE); the bilinear present gave the game its GPU time back as resolution, not frames
# The GPU clock is kept at its top (DM_GPU_KEEP): in fullscreen with Game Mode on and the keeper off it averaged 1,199 MHz of 1,398. About 4.5 W more in a race
# A submission goes to the GPU in segments of 8 draws while the GPU has run out of work (DM_NVN_CUT; default 64), so the GPU starts sooner after the game submits:
# four players, the heaviest minute, 10 and 38 frames off their step with 64, none with 8
# Upload sources are copied into a 128 MB resident ring instead of buffers made resident for each upload (DM_NVN_UP_COPY): a scene cut's residency work halves
